author: Ilana Arougheti
title: Lee's Summit voters face long lines, sites low on ballots ahead of polls closing - NewsBreak
text:
By Ilana Arougheti ,
1 days ago A voter is seen through a ballot magnifier while they cast their vote at Thousand Oaks Oasis Pool and Clubhouse during Election Day on Tuesday, April 7, 2026, in Parkville. Emily Curiel/ecuriel@kcstar.com Voters in Lee’s Summit encountered long lines at the polls Tuesday evening as at least three polling places ran into shortages of preprinted paper ballots, the Jackson County Election Board said.
Ballot shortages were reported at Hawthorne Hill Elementary School, Holy Spirit Catholic Church and Longview Community Center, JCEB Democratic Director Sara Zorich told The Star.
“We got a really good turnout,” Zorich said.
The JCEB prints out hundreds of paper ballots ahead of each election and distributes them to polling places across the metro. When polling places started reporting shortages, the JCEB started printing additional ballots, Zorich said.
However, transporting ballots from the JCEB headquarters in Independence to the affected polling places in Lee’s Summit during evening traffic was a slow process, Zorich said. The JCEB initiated a second response to the shortage by asking voters to use the ADA-compliant alternative polling machines stationed at every poll instead of getting a paper ballot.
The alternative ballot marking devices print out a paper ballot each time they are used, Zorich said, giving some voters another way to obtain one.
“We have techs out in the field, so we knew we could get some of those ADA machines out quicker,” Zorich said. “By the time we got ballots printed and delivered, it was faster to get machines.”
All affected precincts received extra paper ballots before polls closed at 7 p.m. Tuesday, Zorich said.
Tuesday’s primary elections included several high-profile statewide ballot questions and dozens of local races across Kansas and Missouri, including five contested county legislative primaries and a crowded county executive primary.

The JCEB prints out hundreds of paper ballots ahead of each election and distributes them to polling places across the metro.
